title: AS-IS: EU Data Center Site Research — Before the Tool
subtitle: How Jordan finds and evaluates EU DC locations today
trigger: Investment mandate issued — leadership commits to EU expansion at X MW by a defined deadline
end_state: IC / board presentation delivered; site recommendation approved or returned for revision

quantified_costs.in_house_analyst_cost_eur: €18,000–€30,000 (€600–€850/day blended rate × 30–35 days; sources: Stafiz 2025, Consultancy.eu 2025, Metrics.biz 2025, Breagh Recruitment 2026)
quantified_costs.external_consultant_alternative_eur: €40,000–€120,000 per engagement (sources: Aninver feasibility benchmark $20k–$500k; Datarooms.org TDD $75k–$500k; Arcadis 4-DC German contract Nov 2025 implies ~€80k–€240k/engagement)
quantified_costs.decision_risk_lifetime: €50M–€1.7B over 20-year asset life for 50–200 MW DC. EU wholesale spread: €72–73/MWh Nordic vs Italy (AleaSoft 2024, FfE 2024). 100 MW DC annual electricity cost $41M–$131M depending on location (CNBC May 2026). Energy = 40–67% of DC opex (Epoch AI 2026, NetworkInstallers 2026).
quantified_costs.ember_carbon_data_lag: 1–3 months at source: Ember publishes EU country figures with ~1 month lag, some markets up to 3 months. Updates twice monthly (Ember methodology 2025).
quantified_costs.entso_e_granularity: Bidding zone level (~30 zones EU-wide). Most major markets = 1 zone per country: Germany, France, Poland, Netherlands, Belgium are each a single zone. Sub-national nodal prices not publicly available (Synertics 2024, ENTSO-E documentation 2024).
quantified_costs.grid_queue_context: 1,700+ GW waiting in EU grid queues as of 2024 (Eurelectric 2025). Typical grid connection reinforcement: 5–10 years (Eurelectric 2024). EU Grid congestion costs: €4.3B in 2024 (IEA 2025).
quantified_costs.re_run_cost: Each scenario change (different MW or carbon ceiling) requires a full manual rebuild — 1–2 additional analyst days at €600–€850/day

stages.name: Mandate & Brief
stages.description: Leadership issues the directive: EU expansion, known MW target, rough timeline. Jordan receives the brief and scopes the task.
steps: CEO or IC issues EU expansion mandate with MW commitment and deadline
Jordan receives verbal or email brief — MW is fixed, carbon ceiling often TBD or qualitative
Jordan scopes the work: which EU markets to screen, what data is needed, who else is involved
Checks whether any prior analysis exists — rarely reusable; different scope, different format
pain_points: Carbon ceiling stated qualitatively ('we need to be green') — no gCO₂/kWh target defined yet
No structured intake format — scope must be inferred and confirmed through back-and-forth
Prior analysis from previous deals is not reusable — different geography, different assumptions
stages.emotional_state: Energized but scope is underspecified — early ambiguity creates downstream rework

stages.name: Energy Price Data Sourcing
stages.description: Jordan manually pulls wholesale electricity price data from ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, country by country.
steps: Log into ENTSO-E Transparency Platform
Navigate to day-ahead market prices — separate download per country
Download CSVs for up to 20+ candidate EU countries
Clean and normalize: different date formats, units, missing values per country
Merge into master Excel sheet — country-level averages only
pain_points: ENTSO-E organises data by ~30 bidding zones; most major EU markets (Germany, France, Poland, Netherlands) = 1 zone per country — one country-wide average price masks all regional variation
Sub-national nodal price variation — the signal that matters for regional siting — is not publicly available on ENTSO-E
Up to 20+ individual zone/country downloads required — no unified bulk EU export
Format inconsistencies across zones require manual cleaning before any analysis
No forward curve — static historical snapshot only
stages.emotional_state: Mechanical and tedious — high-effort, low-value data wrangling

stages.name: Carbon Intensity Data Sourcing
stages.description: Jordan looks up grid carbon intensity per country from the Ember Climate website — manually, one country at a time.
steps: Navigate to Ember Climate website
Look up grid carbon intensity per country — annual or trailing 12-month averages
Manually transcribe or download — no bulk EU pull available
Note data vintage: figures often 3–12 months stale
Map country averages into master Excel sheet
pain_points: Carbon data is country-averaged only — no zone or NUTS2-level granularity in Ember's published dataset
Publication lag: ~1 month for most EU countries; up to 3 months for some markets (Ember methodology 2025)
Cannot determine which EU zones qualify for a specific gCO₂/kWh ceiling without manual country-by-country filtering
Sub-national variation invisible: northern Germany (wind-heavy) treated identically to coal-heavy east
RE100 compliance check is manual: compare each country figure against policy target one by one
stages.emotional_state: Frustrated — knows zone-level variation exists but has no way to access it

stages.name: Grid Infrastructure Scoping
stages.description: Jordan qualitatively assesses grid infrastructure (substations, fiber) for shortlisted regions using maps and OSM.
steps: Open Google Maps and OpenStreetMap for candidate regions
Visually locate substation markers near shortlisted areas
Check for fiber and telecom infrastructure markers
Qualitatively assess industrial land availability and accessibility
Note findings in spreadsheet — unstructured, no consistent scoring
pain_points: OSM data quality is inconsistent across EU — reliable in DE/NL, sparse in eastern EU
Substation markers show presence but not capacity, voltage level, or available headroom
No way to assess grid congestion risk or spare connection capacity from visual inspection
Fiber coverage proxied by road density — unreliable for DC-grade connectivity decisions
Assessment is qualitative and non-defensible — hard to justify methodology at IC
stages.emotional_state: Uncertain and uncomfortable — knows the infrastructure check is superficial but has no alternative

stages.name: Manual Data Integration & Longlist
stages.description: Jordan stitches energy price, carbon, and grid data into a master spreadsheet and builds a longlist of candidate regions.
steps: Merge ENTSO-E energy price tab, Ember carbon tab, and OSM grid notes into a master sheet
Align geographic levels — country data forced onto regional siting decisions
Assign rough scores manually per candidate region
Produce longlist of 8–12 candidate countries or broad regions
Flag obvious disqualifiers: very high carbon, very high price, known grid issues
pain_points: Data lives at country level — cannot screen at zone level where the DC will actually be located
Manual merge is error-prone: copy-paste mistakes, stale tab versions, unit mismatches
Geographic mismatch: country price averages do not reflect regional nodal variation
Scoring is ad hoc — no defensible weighting methodology or audit trail
Longlist is built on incomplete data — gaps filled by assumption or prior knowledge
stages.emotional_state: Overwhelmed — managing inconsistencies across data of different quality, granularity, and vintage

stages.name: Supply Mix Analysis
stages.description: Jordan builds a power supply mix model (grid / PPA / on-site) for shortlisted regions — in Excel, from scratch, every deal.
steps: For each shortlisted region, research PPA availability and indicative rates
Reach out to network or PPA brokers for indicative pricing — or use stale benchmarks
Estimate curtailment zones qualitatively from industry knowledge and old reports
Build Excel model: grid spot cost, PPA rate, on-site LCOE, blended result per region
Stress-test assumptions manually, one scenario at a time
pain_points: PPA rate data is not public — requires broker network or expensive consultant report
Curtailment zone intelligence does not exist in one place — assembled from industry contacts and old reports
Model rebuilt from scratch on every deal — no reusable template, no institutional memory
LCOE benchmarks used are often 12–24 months stale
PPA discount cannot be quantified at zone level — can flag the opportunity, cannot price it for the CFO
Any change to MW or carbon ceiling requires a full manual rebuild of this model
stages.emotional_state: Frustrated — rebuilding a near-identical model for the third time this year, from memory

stages.name: Site Shortlisting & Scoring
stages.description: Jordan scores 3–5 final candidate sites across cost, carbon, grid, and connectivity dimensions and produces a ranked output.
steps: Select 3–5 final candidate sites from longlist
Apply manual weights to each dimension
Score each site — subjectively, from the assembled data
Rank sites and produce a comparison table
Draft rationale for the top recommendation
pain_points: Scoring weights are arbitrary — no industry standard, no reproducible methodology
Rationale is difficult to defend at IC if challenged on data source or recency
Load estimate change (e.g. 50 MW → 150 MW) requires full scoring rebuild
No audit trail — cannot show how changing a weight shifts the ranking
Connectivity and congestion scores are qualitative — weakest part of the analysis
stages.emotional_state: Anxious — the ranking is defensible only because Jordan built it, not because the methodology is transparent

stages.name: IC / Board Presentation Preparation
stages.description: Jordan formats the analysis into two separate outputs: a technical deck for the CEO and a cost delta summary for the CFO. Both must be reconciled.
steps: Build PowerPoint deck: site ranking, technical rationale, carbon compliance, grid assessment
Build separate Excel cost delta summary for CFO: energy cost differential, PPA opportunity, LCOE per site
Reconcile numbers between both documents — version mismatch risk
Write narrative explanations for each site from scratch
Prepare to defend data sources, recency, and methodology
pain_points: Two separate outputs from one analysis — CEO sees narrative, CFO sees numbers, risk of misalignment in the room
CFO may be working from a different version of the numbers than CEO by meeting day
Formatting and charting takes as long as the underlying analysis itself
Narrative written manually — no structure inherited from the scoring output
Data is 2–4 weeks old by the time the deck is finalized
Cannot re-run if IC asks for a different scenario during the meeting
stages.emotional_state: Exhausted and deadline-pressured — a formatting sprint after weeks of analysis

stages.name: IC Meeting & Follow-up
stages.description: Jordan presents to the investment committee or board. Live Q&A surfaces data gaps. Follow-up scenarios must be prepared offline and may trigger a second meeting.
steps: Present ranked sites, rationale, carbon compliance, and cost differential to IC
Field live questions: 'What is the grid headroom in Poland?', 'What if we go to 200 MW?', 'How recent is this Ember data?'
Acknowledge gaps in real time — 'I will get back to you on that'
Prepare follow-up scenarios offline — 1–3 additional analyst days per IC question
IC approves, defers pending follow-up, or sends back for full rework
pain_points: Cannot re-run live — what-if scenarios require offline work and potentially a second meeting
Data recency challenged in the room — 'this ENTSO-E data is three months old'
Grid headroom and congestion questions cannot be answered with confidence
PPA opportunity flagged but not priced — IC cannot make a financial commitment on a flag alone
If IC requests a different MW or carbon ceiling, the full analysis restarts from S2
Credibility risk if data is challenged and Jordan cannot defend it in real time
stages.emotional_state: Defensive and stressed — prepared but aware that live challenges will expose data gaps
